title: The Heifer and the Ox
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Heifer went up to an Ox, who was straining hard at the plough, and sympathised with him in a rather patronising sort of way on the necessity of his having to work so hard. Not long afterwards there was a festival in the village and every one kept holiday: but, whereas the Ox was turned loose into the pasture, the Heifer was seized and led off to sacrifice. "Ah," said the Ox, with a grim smile, "I see now why you were allowed to have such an idle time: it was because you were always intended for the altar."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the Ox doing when the Heifer approached him?
options: Straining hard at the plough
Resting after a long day
Grazing quietly in the pasture
Being led toward the village

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Heifer speak to the Ox about his hard work?
options: In a rather patronising sort of way
With genuine admiration
With complete indifference
In an angry, scolding tone

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what event took place in the village not long afterwards?
options: A festival, where everyone kept holiday
A drought that dried up the pasture
A market day for selling cattle
A wedding between two farmers' children

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happened to the Ox during the festival?
options: He was turned loose into the pasture
He was made to work even harder than usual
He was led off to sacrifice
He was sold to another village

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happened to the Heifer during the festival?
options: She was seized and led off to sacrifice
She was turned loose into the pasture
She was given extra food as a reward
She was put to work at the plough instead

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Ox react when he learns what happens to the Heifer?
options: He speaks to her with a grim smile
He weeps openly for her
He refuses to speak to her at all
He begs the farmer to spare her

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Ox say he now understands why the Heifer was allowed such an idle time?
options: Her freedom from labor was never a kindness, but a sign she was being kept for sacrifice
He believes farmers always favor heifers over oxen
He realizes the Heifer had secretly been avoiding her share of work
He learns that idle animals are always chosen for festivals

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: An easy life is not always a blessing, and hard labor is not always the worse fate
Heifers are treated more kindly than oxen in every village
Sympathy from others is always sincere and should be trusted
Festivals bring good fortune to all animals involved

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who approached whom at the start of the fable?
options: The Heifer approached the Ox
The Ox approached the Heifer
A farmer approached both of them
Neither approached the other; they met by chance

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Heifer sympathise with the Ox about?
options: The necessity of his having to work so hard
The poor quality of his food
His old age and failing strength
His having to plough alone without help

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Ox say the Heifer was always intended for?
options: The altar
The plough
A life of leisure
Breeding future oxen

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Ox's grim smile suggest about his feelings toward the earlier sympathy the Heifer showed him?
options: He now sees an ironic reversal in their fortunes that undercuts her earlier pity for him
He feels genuine gratitude for her kindness even now
He is relieved that he no longer has to work as hard as before
He is confused about what has just happened to the Heifer

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "patronising" mean in "a rather patronising sort of way"?
options: Treating someone as though they were less capable or important
Speaking with genuine respect and admiration
Offering to help with physical labor
Speaking in a fearful, hesitant manner

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Heifer pities a hardworking Ox, but is herself later led off to sacrifice while the Ox is turned loose to pasture
An Ox and Heifer are both led off to sacrifice together at the festival
A Heifer takes over the Ox's ploughing duties during the festival
The Ox is sacrificed while the Heifer is spared and turned loose
